open_points.subject: ProofResult identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result.” conflicts with “whether a flow version whose proof failed because a binding was not yet accepted can be proven again later — closed by A05 (yes).”
open_points.question: Is a ProofResult identified only by flow_version_id, or is each result a snapshot that also depends on the binding and manifest facts at proof time?
options: One invariant result per flow version
A snapshot value including the proof-time dependencies
A newly issued observation for every proof action
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as a snapshot value whose facts include the proof-time dependency state.

open_points.subject: Try implementation action and TrialExecution
open_points.text: “try an implementation | agent | trial evidence per case” and “A record with no by-field (AdmissionVerdict, TrialExecution, NodeExecution, EffectAttempt apart from its resolved_by, …) names no actor … the request that caused it is told by the record it hangs from … the implementation's submitted_by.”
open_points.question: How does a TrialExecution produced by an explicit try action record which agent requested that try, especially when that agent did not submit the implementation?
options: Add the requesting actor to each TrialExecution
Add a parent trial-run record carrying the requester and grouping its executions
Do not preserve the requester, making try actions unauditable by actor
open_points.default_guess: Create a trial-run entity with the requester and have TrialExecutions belong to it.

open_points.subject: NodeExecution identity
open_points.text: “Identity: value” conflicts with “an attempt's record is issued once” and with TrialExecution's rule that an issued observation is an entity.
open_points.question: Is NodeExecution a value identified by all its facts, or an entity representing the uniquely issued observation at run_id, node_id, map_index and attempt_number?
options: Value
Entity identified by its execution coordinates
Entity with a separately minted identifier
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as an entity identified by its execution coordinates.

open_points.subject: Process restart and unfinished runs
open_points.text: “EffectAttempt … Read by the run's recovery after restart” and “the record written before an effect is sent, so that a crash … leaves a known unknown” do not say what recovery does to a non-final Run, an in_flight EffectAttempt, or a function/read-operation execution interrupted by the crash.
open_points.question: What lifecycle transitions occur at startup for runs and node attempts that were unfinished when the process stopped?
options: Convert in_flight effects to unknown and interrupted non-effects to failures, then recompute the run status
Leave runs and attempts unchanged until an explicit resume action
Automatically retry interrupted non-effects while never retrying effects
End every affected run as failed
open_points.default_guess: Convert in_flight effects to unknown, record interrupted non-effects as failed, and leave the resulting run pending or failed as appropriate.

open_points.subject: Run termination with in-flight branches
open_points.text: “the run ends refused” and “the run ends cancelled; nothing further is sent” are silent about effects or node executions on independent branches that were already in flight.
open_points.question: When cancellation or an owner's refusal makes a run final, what happens to already-sent effects and other executions that have not concluded, and may their records change after the run became final?
options: Allow them to conclude and record their outcomes without reopening the run
Wait for all in-flight work before making the run final
Prevent cancellation or refusal while anything is in flight
Abandon their outcomes and leave their records in their current states
open_points.default_guess: Stop all new sends, allow already-sent work to conclude and be recorded, and keep the run final.

open_points.subject: Capture of failed executions after run end
open_points.text: TrialCase says capture is refused for an execution “whose run was already released, since its spooled files are gone,” while K-10 says every non-failed run's spool is emptied when the run ends, including a run ending refused or cancelled.
open_points.question: Can a failed function execution be captured after its run ended refused or cancelled, and how is capture handled when that execution used files whose spool has already been emptied?
options: Refuse capture whenever required spool bytes no longer exist
Permit capture after any unreleased run and retain those spools too
Permit value-only capture after such endings but refuse capture requiring missing files
Allow capture only from runs whose final status is failed
open_points.default_guess: Permit capture whenever all required inputs still exist; refuse it when required spool bytes have been removed.

open_points.subject: Function inspection and repair context
open_points.text: “inspect functions … | owner, agent | typed description” conflicts or overlaps ambiguously with “For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence; for composition, contracts, bindings and not implementation bodies.”
open_points.question: Which function records and implementation bodies may the general inspect action return, and what product action or request fact distinguishes repair inspection from composition inspection?
options: General inspection can return implementation bodies, with composition using a separate restricted read
Implementation bodies are available only through an explicit repair-context action
Every agent inspection is limited to one slot but the owner may inspect all
K-12 describes advisory context only and imposes no read restriction
open_points.default_guess: Define an explicit repair-context read for one slot; keep composition and general catalogue inspection from returning implementation bodies.

open_points.subject: Digest derivation
open_points.text: “Every content-derived identity and digest in this kernel is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the model's meaning facts” conflicts with “value_digest: of the value's canonical bytes” and with SpooledFile's content_digest for arbitrary file bytes.
open_points.question: Which digests use JCS-encoded model facts, and which digest the underlying value or file bytes directly?
options: All digests hash JCS, with binary content represented inside canonical JSON
Model identities hash JCS while value and file content digests hash their defined canonical or raw bytes
Each digest has an independent derivation rule
open_points.default_guess: Use JCS for structured model identities and structured request/corpus digests, canonical value bytes for value_digest, and raw file bytes for file content_digest.

open_points.subject: Run success with guarded skips
open_points.text: “A node whose every incoming edge is disabled by its guard is not executed and is recorded skipped_by_guard” conflicts ambiguously with “succeeded when every node and output concluded successfully,” because skipped_by_guard is a distinct non-succeeded NodeExecution status.
open_points.question: Can a run whose valid guard outcome skips nodes or flow outputs end succeeded, and what counts as a successfully concluded node or output for that rule?
options: Expected guarded skips count as successful conclusion
Any skipped node or output makes the run failed
A separate final status represents successful execution with skipped results
open_points.default_guess: Treat expected guarded skips as successful conclusions and let the run end succeeded.
